extracted.intended_audience: institutional press officers, science communicators, and science writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for producing and evaluating press releases about scientific research so they accurately represent findings, enable independent reporting, and serve general audiences and journalists. Emphasizes accuracy, accessibility, sourcing, multimedia, and embargo/access norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funded researchers' obligation to share results
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded researchers have an obligation to share their results with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the ethical expectation that researchers (and their institutions) should disseminate findings; implies press releases are a responsibility as part of public accountability for funded work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases should facilitate, not replace, good journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should facilitate, not replace, good journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases must provide accurate, useful material that enables reporters to do independent reporting rather than serving as finished articles; avoid producing copy that encourages 'churnalism.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize access to scientists and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to scientists and information should be maximized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide researcher availability, direct contact info, press kits, and primary-source links so journalists can verify, ask follow-ups, and obtain independent comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect press credentials and embargo norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Press credentials should be respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow accepted embargo practices and treat credentialed journalists appropriately; use reasonable embargo lead times and respect the reciprocal norms of the press community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Match claims to evidence in source paper; distinguish observed from inferred; note study limitations; include effect sizes (absolute, not just relative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every claim in the release is verifiable against the original paper; explicitly label speculative statements; include limitations and provide absolute effect sizes to avoid misleading impressions of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language for general audiences; define technical terms; provide context for results; explain why findings matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so non-specialist readers can understand significance; avoid unexplained jargon; situate results within broader scientific or societal context and state implications clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Name researchers and affiliations; provide journal citation; link to peer-reviewed paper; disclose funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include transparent, specific source information so journalists can find and evaluate the original work and potential conflicts of interest; include direct links and formal citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide high-resolution images cleared for use; captions with context; video where appropriate; diagrams to explain concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply usable multimedia assets that illustrate findings and can be republished; include informative captions that add context rather than just identify subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access (practical press support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researcher available for interviews; press kit with background; embargo with reasonable lead time; direct contact info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sources reachable for journalists, prepare background materials to expedite reporting, and manage embargoes sensibly to allow thorough coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify claims against original paper (for writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify claims against original paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science writers should confirm release claims by reading the paper and checking that the release's assertions are supported by the evidence and analysis presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek independent expert comment (for writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek independent expert comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should obtain outside perspectives to contextualize and critique findings, particularly to assess novelty, limitations, and potential overclaiming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read methods, not just abstract (for writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read methods, not just abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should examine study design, sample size, statistical analysis, and limitations in the methods to accurately assess validity and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose if story originated from press release (for writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose if story originated from press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about source materials helps readers evaluate independence of reporting and reduces appearance of uncritical reproduction of institutional messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid verbatim rewriting ('churnalism') (for writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rewrite verbatim ('churnalism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should produce original reporting and analysis rather than copying release text; use releases as sources while adding verification and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness: include limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should be complete — limitations included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state study limitations and uncertainty rather than omitting caveats that would temper claims; completeness supports accurate interpretation by journalists and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable independent reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A good release enables independent reporting by offering source access and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links, data access, methods details, researcher contact information, and press kits so journalists can independently verify and expand upon the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't oversell: avoid 'breakthrough' or 'cure' language without basis
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should not oversell findings (no breakthrough/cure language without basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hyperbolic framing and dramatic claims that are not supported by the evidence; be conservative in describing implications to prevent misleading coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multimedia to aid explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should provide multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including images, diagrams, or video helps explain methods or results and makes accurate reporting and public comprehension easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A release should come from a credible source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional reputation, transparent sourcing, and clear authoring contribute to perceived trustworthiness; credibility affects uptake by journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect embargo norms
rubrics_metrics.description: A release should respect embargo norms (reasonable lead time, clear terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoes to enable thorough reporting but provide fair lead times and clear conditions; mishandled embargoes can harm relations with the press and impede coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose funding and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state funders and any potential conflicts so journalists and readers can evaluate possible biases or influences on the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide journal citation and link to peer-reviewed paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide journal citation; link to peer-reviewed paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct citation and link allow reporters to access the primary source for verification and deeper understanding; improves transparency and accuracy.
